**The handoff from ordinary ML to PSD is sensitive; no simple fix wins reliably.**
Normalization can change both the ordinary solution handed over and the PSD
path from that solution. Increasing the budget does not recover the three lost
targets. Restricting which ordinary estimates may be reused helps some cases
but loses another. **Keep two-stage provisional; no implementation change here.**

## The three regressions

| Saved case, all N=20 | What the diagnostic isolates | Starting PSD directly |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Ernst, draw 1 | Either ordinary endpoint reaches the target with PSD normalization off; both stall with it on. | Reaches the target in 40 evaluations with normalization on. |
| Ernst, draw 3 | The normalized ordinary stage finds a better unrestricted solution, but that endpoint leads to a worse PSD minimum under either scaling. | Reaches that same worse PSD minimum. |
| High R², draw 7 | Both the ordinary endpoint and PSD scaling matter. Only the old endpoint with PSD normalization off reaches the target. | Converges, but misses the target. |

The two stalled runs reuse ordinary estimates that **failed the accuracy check**,
with large positive and negative variance components. Increasing the PSD budget
from 5,000 to **25,000 evaluations** makes them return much worse objectives and
loadings in the millions. It does not recover the targets. The third regression
already converges, so a larger budget leaves it unchanged.

## Does a stricter handoff help?

We checked one general rule on **all 120 saved datasets**: reuse ordinary
estimates only when they pass convergence; otherwise start PSD from the original
FABIN3-auto start. This is a single-start policy, not multistart.

```{r}
x <- read.csv('results/two-stage-handoff/summary.csv')
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Batch=ifelse(x$batch=='development','Earlier 60','Later 60'),
  `Targets: current → candidate`=paste0(x$baseline_hit,' → ',x$candidate_hit),
  Gains=x$gain, Losses=x$loss, check.names=FALSE),row.names=FALSE)
```

The rule rescues two Ernst cases but loses an earlier weak-marker case that the
rejected ordinary estimate helped solve. It is **not a clear upgrade** on these
already-inspected data. A better unrestricted ML endpoint also need not be a
better PSD starting point—the feasible domains differ.

**Verdict:** retain normalization, leave the two-stage handoff unchanged for now,
and do not promote two-stage as uniformly preferable to direct PSD. Any further
handoff rule needs broader evidence; avoid a magnitude cutoff tailored to these
examples. Direct PSD remains the simpler route, though it also misses targets.
